$schema_note: Machine-readable re-verification of the SoulSystem static audit. Every finding was re-read against the current source at reverified_against_main; statuses are not inherited from the previous register or from SECURITY_INVARIANTS.md. Paths are repository-relative. Line numbers are deliberately omitted from evidence fields because they go stale; evidence cites files and symbols instead.
method: Static re-verification against current main: each finding's cited code was re-read in the working tree; reachability was established from the soulsystem binary entry points (src/main.rs, src/lib.rs module declarations) and by workspace-wide ripgrep inventories cross-referenced with cargo metadata package roots, excluding the untracked-by-workspace os-agents/ and soullink-node/ duplicate trees. Cited regression tests were confirmed to exist by symbol search and executed for every FIXED_AND_VERIFIED finding. Findings marked REQUIRES_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION need dynamic confirmation that static reading cannot supply.

status_legend.CONFIRMED_CURRENT: Defective behaviour still exists and is reachable; carries reachable_from and reproducer.
status_legend.PARTIALLY_FIXED: A meaningful correction landed but the full invariant is not held; carries remaining_exposure and follow_up.
status_legend.FIXED_AND_VERIFIED: Root cause removed on the production-reachable path and proven by a current in-tree test; carries fixing_prs and verification_tests.
status_legend.NOT_REACHABLE: Defective code still exists but no supported production entry point reaches it; carries unreachable_because.
status_legend.FALSE_POSITIVE: The original claim was factually incorrect.
status_legend.REQUIRES_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION: Static inspection cannot decide; the required dynamic test is stated.
status_legend.DEFERRED_PRODUCT_DECISION: Remaining work needs an explicit product/governance decision; carries decision_required.

findings.title: Unsandboxed Tool Dispatch in Live Agent Path
original_reachable_path: AutonomousAgent::run_react -> async_dispatch_tool -> dispatch_tool -> execute_shell -> bare std::process::Command
findings.current_state: The original vector is closed: soul_tools::execute_shell constructs a soul_sandbox::Sandbox and no bare Command remains on the agent tool-dispatch path. Re-examined more precisely at this commit, correcting an overstatement in the previous re-verification: of the three process-execution sites in src/self_healer.rs, only ONE was ever live. `read_system_stats` ran `df --output=pcent` on every tick of the 30-second run() loop spawned from src/main.rs. The KillNonEssential and RestartService arms exec `kill` and `systemctl`, but no producer in the workspace constructs either DefenseAction variant - Preservation emits only Throttle, MemoryDump, EmergencySave, LocalFallback, DistressSignal and GracefulShutdown - so those two arms were latent, not attacker-reachable as previously described. Both classes are now addressed: the df exec is replaced by a statvfs(3) call (SelfHealer::root_disk_used_percent), removing the spawn entirely rather than sandboxing it; `kill(1)` is replaced by a direct libc::kill signal; and both privileged arms are gated behind ProcessControl::Enabled, which defaults to Disabled, so adding a producer cannot by itself turn bus traffic into host process control. The systemctl unit name is additionally validated by is_safe_service_name. tests/architecture_process_execution.rs now pins the permitted set of process-spawning files in the soulsystem binary crate and fails CI on any new one. P1-8 widens the architecture guard from the binary crate to EVERY workspace member, with each of the 30 production spawn files classified into one of five categories: sandbox-implementation (the crate IS the isolation boundary - bound-system, soul_sandbox, avid-sandbox, soul-kernel/sandbox), host-control-fixed-argv (systemctl/nvidia-smi/ss/df/tmux/docker with no caller-controlled argv), dev-tooling (cargo/git in self-modification and workflow paths), unsandboxed-arbitrary-command (12 files - KNOWN PROBLEMS recorded so they cannot grow, not approvals), and no-reachable-caller. Member directories are parsed from the root Cargo.toml rather than hardcoded, so a new workspace crate is scanned automatically. A false positive is explicitly exempted: soul_sandbox/src/seccomp.rs matches on `execve` only because it names SYS_execve as the syscall it BLOCKS, and a test asserts the exemption stays sound. Verified negatively three ways: an introduced Command in a non-allowlisted crate is caught; breaking the member parsing fails two vacuity guards; a stale allowlist entry is caught.
findings.remaining_exposure: 5 workspace files still perform unsandboxed arbitrary command execution and are recorded in the guard's allowlist rather than fixed. P1-8-B has fixed six sites across three rounds: the request-reachable orchestrator spawn route; the sh -c group (soullink-workflow node and conditions, soullink-actions' shell tool, soul-kernel's Action::ExecuteShell); and soul-bridge's two MCP child spawns. One further entry, soul-kernel/parallel, was RECATEGORISED rather than fixed: `run_action` matches two string literals and spawns `sync` or a fixed `systemctl list-units`, so no caller input reaches argv and `host-control-fixed-argv` is the accurate label. That drop in the budget reflects a corrected label, not work done. What remains: soul-kernel's OptimizeSystem (three FIXED privileged sh -c strings the sandbox would refuse outright - they want rewriting as direct operations, not wrapping), soul-kernel/perception, soul_automation, soullink-orchestrator's main, and soul_gateway's macOS-only osascript iMessage provider (the isolation hook is Linux-specific, so that one needs a decision rather than a mechanical fix). A further 112 spawn sites sit in ten non-member trees that `cargo build --workspace` never builds, so this guard says nothing about them.
findings.required_invariant: No production-reachable code path invokes process execution outside the approved soul_sandbox executor (INV-EXEC-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR D-1): route the agent execution path through the sandbox (CRIT-001)

findings.residual_risk: Agent tool dispatch is sandboxed and tested, the binary's only live unsandboxed spawn is gone, and new ones in src/ now fail CI. Workspace-wide enforcement, and the soul-automodify / iMessage spawns, remain open.
findings.follow_up: P1-8-B: route the 12 unsandboxed-arbitrary-command sites through soul_sandbox, lowering UNSANDBOXED_ARBITRARY_BUDGET with each, starting with soullink-orchestrator-standalone/src/routes/spawn.rs because it is request-reachable. findings.title: Unknown Tool Fallthrough Creates Arbitrary Executable Dispatch
original_reachable_path: AutonomousAgent::run_react -> async_dispatch_tool -> dispatch_tool wildcard `_ =>` -> execute_shell
findings.current_state: dispatch_tool_in resolves the name through ToolId::from_name before any handler is selected; from_name matches the six registered identifiers byte-for-byte (no trimming, case-folding or Unicode normalisation) and returns ToolError::UnknownTool otherwise. The remaining `_ =>` arm in async_dispatch_tool sits AFTER from_name has already succeeded, so it is a wildcard over the validated ToolId enum, not over caller-supplied strings; it delegates to dispatch_tool, which re-validates. There is no path from an unregistered name to process execution.
findings.required_invariant: An unregistered tool name can only produce UnknownTool; it can never reach process execution (INV-TOOL-1).

findings.residual_risk: Registered process tools still depend on the sandbox guarantees tracked under CRIT-001/HIGH-003. Adding a new ToolId variant that maps to execution remains a code-review concern rather than a test-enforced one.

findings.title: Arbitrary Filesystem Writes Without Path Restrictions
original_reachable_path: write_file/patch_file tool -> std::fs::write with caller-controlled absolute path
findings.current_state: FsPolicy::new canonicalises the declared root; resolve_read/resolve_write canonicalise the nearest existing ancestor of the requested path and reject anything that escapes the root, which closes both `..` traversal and symlink escape (including a symlinked directory ancestor). Writes go through atomic_write (temp + rename).
findings.required_invariant: File tools cannot write outside their declared canonical root; symlink escape and check-then-open races are prevented (INV-FS-1/2/4).

findings.title: Unauthenticated State-Changing Gateway/API Routes (auth middleware still absent; production now fail-closed by startup guard)
original_reachable_path: axum router -> state-changing /v1 handlers with no authentication middleware
findings.current_state: soul_gateway::router applies require_auth as a route_layer over every /v1/* operator route, comparing the bearer token with constant_time_eq and failing closed when unconfigured. /health is intentionally unauthenticated. The ws_bridge half is now also fail-closed: WsBridgeConfig gained UnauthenticatedAccess (default Deny), so with no usable shared secret handle_connection refuses the connection before the WebSocket handshake instead of initialising `authenticated = true` as it previously did; a blank or whitespace-only secret is treated as unset by effective_secret() so a misconfigured empty value cannot become a credential; and the token comparison now uses a constant-time equality rather than `token == secret`, closing a timing side channel that the gateway had already closed for its bearer token. src/prod_guard.rs no longer hardcodes the bridge's posture: assemble_posture receives the real WsBridgeConfig and reports authenticated exactly when a usable secret is configured, so production startup aborts with an UnauthenticatedListener violation while the bridge is unauthenticated. Serving without authentication now requires the operator to set SOULSYSTEM_WS_BRIDGE_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED, and that opt-in is deliberately NOT reported as authentication. P1-9 closes the last unauthenticated production listener: src/api.rs now applies its own fail-closed bearer middleware (api::ApiAuth, SOULSYSTEM_API_TOKEN) to every route except /health. That listener exposed /api/exec (shell execution via BoundSystem) and /api/pty/* (interactive terminals) with no authentication of any kind, mitigated only by its 127.0.0.1:9023 bind - which does not protect against another user on the host or a browser-driven request from a page the operator loaded. /metrics is inside the authenticated set because it is a disclosure route. A blank token is treated as unset; the comparison is constant-time; Debug never renders the token. prod_guard::assemble_posture no longer hardcodes the api listener's posture to false - it derives it from the real ApiAuth, which also means production startup can now actually be satisfied on that listener (before this change the hardcoded false made an unauthenticated-listener violation unconditional, so production could never start regardless of configuration). P1-9-B adds per-scope authorization on both listeners, sharing one model (soul_gateway::scope) so the two cannot drift on what a scope means. Scope::{Read,Write,Exec,Admin}; scopes deliberately do NOT imply one another apart from Admin, because implication is easy to get subtly wrong and hard to audit. Exec is separated from Write specifically because it is the scope that turns a leaked token into host compromise. The requirement is declared per route group via a route_layer rather than checked inside handlers, and a source-reading guard test on each listener fails if a route is declared outside every scoped group - it caught a real gap (/v1/stream) on first run. Insufficient scope returns 403, not 401, so a client is not invited to retry with credentials that would fail identically; authentication is still checked first, so an anonymous caller cannot learn which scope a route needs.
findings.remaining_exposure: Per the recorded product decision, a credential configured without a scope list is granted every scope, so scopes are OPT-IN. This makes least privilege expressible, not default: a deployment that does not configure scopes is exactly as exposed as before, and one compromised unscoped token still yields full operator power including shell execution. The invariant therefore is not held by the mechanism existing - it is held only once a deployment narrows its tokens, which this repository cannot prove.
findings.required_invariant: Every state-changing endpoint requires authentication and an authorization scope (INV-NET-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR F): mandatory gateway authentication + webhook fail-closed (CRIT-007)

findings.residual_risk: Authentication is complete and fails closed on every production listener, and authorization is now expressible with a shared scope model enforced per route. The residual is that the opt-in default leaves an unconfigured deployment all-or-nothing, so the property depends on operator configuration rather than on code.
findings.follow_up: Optional hardening once operators have adopted scopes: have the production startup guard report, or refuse, a credential that holds Admin, converting the opt-in default into an explicit per-deployment acknowledgement.

findings.title: Secrets Never Zeroized (SecretsCrypto master_key is plain Vec<u8>)
original_reachable_path: SecretsCrypto::master_key held as a plain Vec<u8>, never zeroized on drop
findings.current_state: master_key is a secrecy::Secret (zeroized on drop) and derive_key returns Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, so derived key material is wiped as well. P1-5 adds soulsystem_common::secrets::SecretString, whose Debug, Display AND Serialize all render a fixed redaction, so an enclosing #[derive(Debug)] is safe without its author having to think about it - the accidental path, which is the one that actually happens, is removed rather than discouraged. The redaction is a fixed string, not a length-derived mask, because `***` versus `****************` discloses the length. Serialize deliberately writes the redaction too: a config struct is routinely serialized to a debug endpoint or a state dump, and round-tripping plaintext through those is the same leak in a different coat. Five structs are migrated: WsBridgeConfig::shared_secret, LlmConfig::auth_token, OpenclawConfig::auth_token, DiscordWebhookBody::token (an inbound webhook body is exactly what gets logged when parsing fails), and - most importantly - soullink-security's scanner Finding::secret, which derived Debug AND Serialize over the very credential it had just detected, beside a `masked` field that existed because someone already knew displaying it was unsafe. A workspace-wide guard (tests/architecture_secret_types.rs) fails on any new secret-named String field on a Debug-deriving struct.
findings.required_invariant: Secrets use redacting/zeroizing types; Debug/Display never reveal them (INV-SEC-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR J): zeroize secret key material in soullink-secrets (fixes HIGH-001)

findings.residual_risk: Zeroization and OS-store lifecycle are in place, and P1-5/P1-5-B completed the type sweep: no credential remains in a plain `String` on a `Debug`-deriving struct in any workspace member, with the guard's budget at 0. Two of the migrated fields needed a distinct type - `HelloOk::device_token` and `AuthInfo::token` are WebSocket handshake fields whose serialization is their purpose, so they use `ProtocolSecret` (redacting Debug/Display, faithful Serialize); a redacting Serialize there would have broken authentication at runtime with no compile error. Residual: the guard keys on `#[derive(Debug)]` and on field names. Structs holding credentials while deriving only `Clone` (`clawd::Settings`, `soul-dashboard::AppState`) are not reported, and a credential in a field named `value` or `bot` is invisible to name matching - `synergie::Telegram::bot` was migrated only because a call site led there, not because the guard found it.
findings.follow_up: P1-5-C: extend the guard to Clone-only credential holders and to a check that does not depend on field naming.
findings.remaining_exposure: 16 structs across workspace members still hold credentials in plain String fields on Debug-deriving types, recorded in the guard's NOT_YET_MIGRATED list with a two-way count budget: AVID's four provider/config structs and its scout AuthMethod enum, the brain gateway's ProviderConfig/TokenInfo/HelloOk/AuthInfo, soullink-proxy's ProxyConfig, synergie's two config structs, souls' LlmPersistConfig, soulsystem-multiagent's SpecializedAgent, avid-intel's MonitorConfig and soul_api's TelegramBot. Two further limitations are stated rather than counted as clean: the guard keys on #[derive(Debug)], so a credential-holding struct deriving only Clone (clawd::Settings, soul-dashboard::AppState both do) is not reported - a smaller exposure, not an absent one, since it still leaks via a hand-written Display, via serde, or the moment somebody adds Debug; and the match is name-based, so a credential in a field called `value` or `blob` will not be found by any amount of this.

findings.title: soul_sandbox provides string-filtering + optional seccomp only, not OS-level isolation; reachable with no-seccomp default policy
original_reachable_path: soul_sandbox applied string filtering and an optional seccomp profile only; no OS-level isolation
findings.current_state: Real OS-level controls now exist. seccomp is on by default (SandboxPolicy::default().seccomp_profile is Some("default")) and fails closed: install_filter errors propagate out of pre_exec and abort the fork before exec. PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS is set unconditionally first, so the filter installs for unprivileged callers, not only root. Output is bounded by max_output_bytes (2 MiB default) via read_capped, and the process group is killed on timeout. Network isolation via unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET) is deliberately best-effort: on hosts where AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces (Ubuntu 23.10+, GitHub Actions runners) it logs and continues rather than blocking all execution. P1-3 adds CPU, memory, file-descriptor, file-size and core bounds via setrlimit(2) in the same pre_exec seam (ResourceLimits; defaults RLIMIT_AS 4 GiB, RLIMIT_NOFILE 256, RLIMIT_CPU 60 s, RLIMIT_FSIZE 256 MiB, RLIMIT_CORE 0). Both the soft and the hard limit are lowered, so the child cannot raise its own soft limit back, and the desired value is clamped to the inherited hard limit so a tighter host ceiling is preserved rather than causing EPERM. This path is fail-closed: lowering an rlimit needs no privilege and has no host-policy dependency, so a failure aborts the fork before exec. setrlimit rather than cgroups because cgroup v2 requires root or a delegated subtree, which the unprivileged deployments this targets do not have.
findings.remaining_exposure: Pids remain unbounded by default: RLIMIT_NPROC is counted per real UID rather than per process tree, so enabling it by default would make the first fork of an ordinary command fail with EAGAIN on any shared-UID host while not bounding a determined caller. It is available as ResourceLimits::max_processes and proven to reach the child, but is only safe under a dedicated UID; a cgroup pids.max is the correct control otherwise, and is not implemented. RLIMIT_AS bounds virtual address space rather than resident memory. Mount and PID namespaces are still not applied, so the filesystem view and process table are shared - CLONE_NEWPID in particular cannot be added as a flag, because unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) affects only children created afterwards and pre_exec execs rather than forks, so it needs a double-fork restructure of the spawn model. Network isolation is still not guaranteed: on a restricted host the command runs with full host network access.
findings.required_invariant: Process tools run under OS-level isolation with bounded resources and no network by default (INV-EXEC-2/3/4).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR D-2): fail-closed seccomp + network namespace isolation

findings.residual_risk: CPU, memory, fd and file-size exhaustion are now bounded on every Unix host; process-count exhaustion is not, unless the sandbox runs under a dedicated UID. Network isolation silently degrades, which is the documented and intended trade-off but still means egress cannot be relied upon as a control.
findings.follow_up: Roadmap P1-12: a cgroup v2 backend for pids.max/memory.max where a delegated subtree exists, the double-fork spawn restructure needed for CLONE_NEWPID, a filesystem-view policy before CLONE_NEWNS is useful, and per-tool egress allowlisting instead of all-or-nothing network isolation.

findings.title: CCOS Memory Uses Non-Atomic Persistence
original_reachable_path: CCOS write_json / KernelSnapshot::save -> std::fs::write (truncate-in-place, torn write on crash)
findings.current_state: Both CCOS persistence entry points now call util::write_durable, which writes to a temporary file, fsyncs, and renames over the target.
findings.required_invariant: CCOS and other durable stores use atomic writes (INV-PERSIST-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR L): route CCOS persistence.rs/persist.rs through atomic write_durable

findings.residual_risk: Each file is individually atomic, and P1-7 added set-level detection on top: a manifest written last records a SHA-256 digest per member file, so a crash between the three renames leaves digests that no longer match and the tear is detected on load rather than silently accepted. State versioning is present (`format_version`, refused if newer than this build understands). What remains is that detection is not repair: a torn set is refused, with no rollback to the previous generation, so the process cannot start until an operator restores a backup. A directory with no manifest is also accepted as legacy so upgrades are not stranded, which means anyone able to unlink the manifest can downgrade a directory to unverified; `restore_runtime_strict` refuses that but is opt-in and has no production caller yet. P1-7-B added RECOVERY on top of that detection: `save_state` snapshots the outgoing verified generation into `state.prev` before overwriting anything, and `restore_runtime_repairing` falls back to it when the live set is torn. This is recovery, not reconstruction - the interrupted generation is gone and n-1 takes its place, so a repair LOSES THE MOST RECENT SAVE. That is why it is a separate call rather than something `restore_runtime` does silently: a caller who would rather investigate a tear than lose a generation must be able to choose. Only a verified set is snapshotted, so a save over an already-torn set leaves the older good fallback intact rather than replacing it with the newer broken one. Disk cost: the state directory roughly doubles.
findings.follow_up: P1-7-C: two gaps remain. (1) Strict restore is still opt-in and no production caller uses it, so a DELETED manifest is still indistinguishable from one that never existed - making strict the default needs a migration window, which is a deployment decision and is being asked rather than assumed. (2) Backup qualification still covers only the CCOS three-file state directory; the provenance index added by P1-6-B and the other durable stores have no equivalent backup/restore test.

findings.current_state: soul_entity/src/entity.rs still reports plan execution with the literal feedback string "Plan execute avec succes (simulation)" rather than performing or verifying real execution, and the autonomous loop advances on a tokio::time::sleep tick. src/main.rs declares an `entity` CLI flag documented as 'Start the unified autonomous entity (SoulEntity + gateway + skills)' and imports SoulEntity, so the path is reachable in a supported build.

findings.reproducer: Inspect soul_entity/src/entity.rs: the success feedback string is a compile-time constant containing '(simulation)' and is not derived from any executor result. Run the binary with --entity and observe plans reported successful without a corresponding tool invocation.

findings.title: Webhook Verifications Lenient When Secrets Unset
original_reachable_path: POST /providers/*/webhook accepted unsigned payloads when the provider secret was unset
findings.current_state: Both halves are now closed. The handlers still fail closed when a provider secret is unset (PR F), and a configured deployment now cryptographically verifies the request. The handlers previously used axum's Json(payload) extractor, which consumes the body - signature verification requires the raw bytes, so they now take HeaderMap + Bytes, verify, and only then deserialize via parse_verified_body. Per provider, verified against the actual scheme rather than the roadmap's shorthand: Discord uses Ed25519 (NOT HMAC) over `timestamp || body` with DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY as a hex public key; Slack uses HMAC-SHA256 over the base string `v0:{timestamp}:{body}`; Meta/WhatsApp uses HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body via X-Hub-Signature-256. HMAC comparisons use subtle::ConstantTimeEq; Ed25519 verification is constant-time by construction. Timestamp freshness is enforced within MAX_SKEW (5 minutes, both directions) for Discord and Slack; Meta sends no timestamp, so replay protection carries that weight alone for WhatsApp. A ReplayCache on GatewayState rejects any signature already accepted, evicting entries older than MAX_SKEW so it stays bounded. Every rejection reason returns one opaque 401 and is logged server-side only, so a caller cannot distinguish a bad signature from a stale timestamp and probe the difference.
findings.required_invariant: Webhooks fail closed when a secret is unset and reject invalid/replayed signatures (INV-NET-3).

fixing_prs.title: security(P1-1): verify webhook signatures, freshness and replay (implementation commit; the merge commit will differ)

findings.residual_risk: Verification is unit-tested against signatures generated with the real algorithms, including genuine Ed25519 signing, rather than mocks. It has not been exercised against live traffic from the three providers, so a header-name or encoding mismatch would only surface in a real integration. The replay cache is per-process and in-memory: a multi-instance deployment behind a load balancer would not share it, so a captured request could be replayed once per instance within the freshness window.

findings.title: soul_llm makes a single HTTP attempt with no retry/backoff on transient LLM provider failures
original_reachable_path: run_react -> guarded_llm_chat -> LlmClient -> single provider HTTP attempt; any transient failure aborts the turn
findings.current_state: CORRECTION to this register's own earlier text, which said only that nothing acted on RateLimited: nothing ever CONSTRUCTED it either. No provider inspected the HTTP status at all - every call was .send().await?.json().await?, so a 429 or 503 reached serde_json as an error page and surfaced as LlmError::Serialization. Retry classification would have been reading the wrong signal, so both halves land together. All 16 provider request sites now go through http::SendChecked::send_checked, which maps status onto a classified error in one place (429 -> RateLimited with Retry-After, 5xx -> ServiceUnavailable, 401/403 -> Auth, other 4xx -> Provider) and parses Retry-After in both RFC 9110 forms (seconds and HTTP-date). LlmClient::with_retry then applies a bounded RetryPolicy - 3 attempts, 500ms initial, 30s ceiling, x2, equal jitter - to generate, chat and stream establishment. A server-supplied Retry-After overrides the curve; one longer than max_backoff stops rather than parking the run or retrying early. The concurrency permit is held across attempts (retries are one logical request) and the token budget is charged once.
reachable_from: soul-agent-core run_react -> guarded_llm_chat -> LlmClient::generate_with_goal -> provider generate (single attempt)
findings.reproducer: Inspect soul_llm/src/client.rs and soul_llm/src/providers/*.rs for a retry construct: the only sleep is within the test module. A provider returning 429 or a transient 5xx surfaces directly to the caller and ends the agent turn.
findings.required_invariant: Transient provider failures are retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, honouring Retry-After.

fixing_prs.title: security(P1-4): retry provider calls with bounded backoff, and classify HTTP status first (implementation commit; the merge commit will differ)

findings.residual_risk: The provider layer now absorbs transient failures. Three bounded gaps remain and are not claimed as closed: only stream ESTABLISHMENT is retried, because once a chunk may have reached the caller a re-run would duplicate output rather than recover; the retry budget is per-call, so a caller in a loop can still issue many bounded sequences; and no circuit breaker trips after repeated exhaustion, so a hard-down provider is re-probed on every call. Verification is against a failure-injecting mock provider and a local socket serving raw 429/503/401 responses, not against live provider traffic.
findings.follow_up: Circuit-breaker partitioning per provider (separate finding); agent-loop consumption of RetriesExhausted is roadmap P1-13.

findings.required_invariant: soul_llm bounds the number of outbound provider requests in flight, independent of token-budget accounting (INV-PROVIDER-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR M): request-level concurrency cap for soul_llm (fixes MED-002)

The genuinely varied vectors in soullink-reasoning/src/tree.rs are inside #[test] functions only.

findings.reproducer: Read the ToT branch in soul-agent-core/src/lib.rs: query_emb and thought_emb are both vec![1.0_f32; 64]. Their cosine similarity is identically 1.0, so evaluate_node returns the same score for every leaf and NodeStatus::Pruned is never selected on merit.
findings.required_invariant: Reasoning-quality scores that drive pruning must be computed from real semantic embeddings, or the feature must not claim to prune on merit (INV-TRUTH-1).
findings.residual_risk: Tree-of-Thoughts advertises semantic search but performs none; branch selection is effectively arbitrary while appearing principled, which can mislead operators and any evaluation built on it.
findings.follow_up: Wire real embeddings (soullink-eval or the configured embedding provider) into the ToT branch, or gate the strategy off and stop reporting semantic scores.

findings.title: Inconsistent Retry Policy: fabricated tool success rates + strategy-less auto_repair
original_reachable_path: strategy selection consumed a fabricated success rate (always 1.0) and auto_retry had no strategy-level policy
findings.current_state: The fabricated-success-rate half is fixed by PR #80: success_rate() is computed from really-recorded outcomes and strategy_selector.record_outcome receives a real StrategyOutcome. The retry-policy half is unchanged: there is still no single coherent retry policy - soul_llm performs no provider retry at all (MED-001), while the agent loop retries at the strategy level, so retry behaviour differs by layer with no shared budget or backoff. P1-4 supplies the mechanism for the coordination half: LlmError::is_retryable is one classification both layers can consult instead of maintaining divergent opinions, and LlmError::RetriesExhausted { attempts, last } lets an outer layer distinguish 'failed once, transiently' from 'the provider layer already backed off and retried N times'. soul_llm now performs real bounded retry, so MED-001's half of the gap is closed. P1-13-B completed the consumption: the ReAct loop now calls guarded_llm_chat_typed and branches on ProviderOutcome. Exhausted and Permanent ABORT rather than replan - self-repair cannot reach a provider that is down, and replanning asks the same dead endpoint a different question; Retryable and BreakerOpen keep the previous self-repair path, since the breaker's own state handles the backoff. AgentConfig::max_provider_attempts (default 12) is one ceiling across both layers, and the provider layer's OWN attempt count is charged against it, which is what makes the two budgets sum rather than multiply: N strategy attempts each costing M provider attempts would otherwise be N*M requests to a hard-down provider. ProviderOutcome::classify was extracted so the tests exercise the same code the loop runs - P1-13's tests mirrored the match, and a drifted mirror of a retry decision passes while the decision is wrong.
findings.required_invariant: Retry policy is coherent across layers and driven by real outcome data.

fixing_prs.title: security(PR I): record actual tool outcome in planner history (fixes HIGH-009)

findings.residual_risk: The ceiling is per `run_task` run and is not shared across concurrent runs or across agents, so K parallel agents can each spend the full budget against one provider. `guarded_llm_chat` (the String-returning path) still exists and is used by the second call site at the reflection step, which does not branch on the outcome - a failure there still surfaces as an untyped error.
findings.follow_up: MED-009-B: route the reflection call site through the typed path too, and consider whether the attempt ceiling should be shared across concurrent runs rather than per-run.
findings.remaining_exposure: The ReAct loop's main call site is done, but the SECOND call site - the reflection step at `guarded_llm_chat(&messages, ...)` - still uses the String-returning path and does not branch on the outcome, so a failure there surfaces as an untyped error and is not charged against the shared ceiling. The ceiling is also per `run_task` run and not shared across concurrent runs or agents, so K parallel agents can each spend the full budget against one provider. Neither is a hot loop; both are uncoordinated spend.

findings.title: Quarantined tool output was ingested into the CCOS causal graph, erasing the file's existing record
findings.discovered_by: P1-6 provenance work, not the original audit; found while establishing what a persisted record carries.
original_reachable_path: run_react -> tool dispatch -> screen_tool_output (Malicious -> quarantine placeholder) -> record_tool_outcome -> ccos_observe_tool -> CcosMemory::ingest_source(uri, placeholder)
findings.current_state: Fixed. CRIT-005's fix routed tool output through the injection scanner before persistence, and malicious output was replaced with a quarantine placeholder. That placeholder was then passed to `CcosMemory::ingest_source` for the file's uri. `ingest_source` REPLACES a file node's parsed contents, and the placeholder parses to zero symbols, so the write did not store a redaction over the previous record - it removed the file from the causal graph altogether (measured: a file recalled as 2 items before the quarantined read recalls as 0 after). The `IngestReport` was discarded with `let _ =`, so nothing surfaced. An attacker able to append an injection payload to a file the agent had already ingested therefore had a silent primitive for deleting that file from the agent's causal memory on the next read, degrading recall for the code under attack. `ccos_observe_tool` now checks `TrustLevel::is_persistable()` and refuses the write, leaving the existing record intact and emitting a SafetyWarning; the refusal is recorded in the provenance log rather than being silent.
findings.required_invariant: Screened-but-refused content must never be written to a content store in place of the record it would displace; a refusal must be observable.

fixing_prs.title: security(P1-6): carry provenance and trust on persisted memory, and stop quarantine from erasing the causal graph (implementation commit; the merge commit will differ)

findings.residual_risk: The refusal protects the causal graph's content. It does not give the operator a durable record of which paths were attacked: the provenance log is in-process and bounded (512 entries), so across a restart or a long run the fact that a given file produced quarantined output is lost. The SafetyWarning event is emitted at the time but is not persisted anywhere by this crate.
findings.follow_up: P1-6-B: durable, store-side provenance so a trust level survives restart and eviction.

findings.title: synergie's HTTP API allowed every cross-origin caller by default, on a surface whose auth token also defaults to None
findings.discovered_by: P1-10 CORS sweep; not in the original audit, and not among the four services the roadmap listed for P1-10.
original_reachable_path: synergie serve -> api::serve -> ApiCfg::cors_allow_any defaulted true -> CorsLayer::new().allow_origin(Any) applied to /status and the WS API
findings.current_state: Fixed. `ApiCfg::cors_allow_any` carried `#[serde(default = "default_true")]` AND was `true` in the `Default` impl, so a config that omitted the field - or no config file at all - served `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. `ApiCfg::auth_token` defaults to `None` on the same struct, so the permissive header sat in front of an unauthenticated API. The defect was spelled `.allow_origin(Any)` rather than `CorsLayer::permissive()`, which is why a search for the latter did not find it and why the roadmap's list of four affected services was short by three. Replaced with `cors_origins: Vec<String>` defaulting to empty, evaluated through the shared `soul_cors::CorsPolicy`, which fails closed. `cors_allow_any` is still parsed so an existing config is not silently reinterpreted, but it is not honoured and logs a warning naming the replacement.
findings.required_invariant: A listener that has not been configured must not be the most permissive one on the network; an insecure setting must not be reachable by omission.

fixing_prs.title: security(P1-10): one fail-closed CORS policy, and a guard that found three more services (implementation commit; the merge commit will differ)

findings.residual_risk: The architecture guard covers workspace members only. `os-agents/soul_gateway` is outside the workspace and still calls `CorsLayer::permissive()` (LOW-003). The guard is also syntactic: an allowlist assembled at runtime from an attacker-influenced source would not be visible to it. synergie itself remains unauthenticated by default (`auth_token: None`); this finding closed the cross-origin exposure, not the missing authentication.
findings.follow_up: P1-10-B: fold soul_gateway's and soul-dashboard's P1-2 policies into soul-cors so one implementation remains; separately, decide whether synergie's API should require a token by default.

findings.title: POST /api/mesh/spawn turns an unauthenticated request body into a process, with argument injection into the spawned interpreter and no ceiling on how many
findings.audit_category: Missing Authentication / Argument Injection / Resource Exhaustion
findings.discovered_by: P1-8-B. The site was already recorded in the INV-EXEC-1 allowlist as the one entry reachable from an HTTP route; reading it closely for the fix turned up three distinct defects, only one of which was the one the roadmap named.
original_reachable_path: POST /api/mesh/spawn -> route_spawn -> body["domain"] -> tokio::process::Command::new("python3").arg(script).arg("--brain").arg(domain).spawn()
findings.current_state: Partially fixed. Three defects were real and are fixed; a fourth is a deployment decision and is not. What was NOT wrong: this was never shell injection. argv was built from discrete `.arg()` calls and no shell was involved, so `;` and `$(...)` in `domain` were inert. Routing the joined string through `Sandbox::execute` - which is what 'route it through soul_sandbox' would literally mean - would have made this worse, because `build_command` splits on whitespace, so a domain containing a space would have become two argv elements where it had been one. (1) ARGUMENT INJECTION, fixed: `domain` was the value of `--brain`, so a domain of `--config=/etc/shadow` reaches brain_v12.py's argument parser as a flag, not a value. Now rejected twice independently - by `valid_domain`'s allowlist charset at the route, and by `SpawnSpec::value`, which refuses any caller-supplied argument beginning with `-`. (2) UNBOUNDED SPAWNING, fixed: every request forked an interpreter that nothing reaped or counted against a ceiling; `increment_spawn_count` fed a metrics endpoint and bounded nothing. Now capped at MAX_LIVE_BRAINS=16, and a brain that fails its health check has its process group killed rather than being left running. (3) NO ISOLATION, fixed: the child inherited privileges, fds, rlimits and network in full. Now spawned via the new `Sandbox::spawn_supervised`, which applies the same setpgid + setrlimit + seccomp pre_exec hook as every other sandboxed path. `network_isolated` is explicitly false and documented, because a brain exists to bind a port and answer on it - that is a real and deliberate reduction relative to the default policy, not an oversight. (4) NO AUTHENTICATION, NOT fixed: the route has no auth layer. soul_cors (P1-10) makes a browser's cross-origin call fail, but CORS is not authentication and stops nothing that is not a browser - curl reaches this route regardless. Whether this service should require a token is a deployment decision about how it is meant to be exposed, so it is recorded rather than answered. Also fixed in passing: the port search was `while used.contains(&port) { port += 1 }` on a u16 with no bound, which overflows past 65535 - a debug panic, or a release wrap to port 0, which means 'any free port' and would leave the health check polling the wrong one. And a `.unwrap()` on the reqwest client builder would have killed the supervising task, and with it the only handle to the child.
findings.residual_risk: The route remains unauthenticated, so any client that can reach the listener can spawn up to MAX_LIVE_BRAINS processes. The cap turns an unbounded host-level denial of service into a bounded one; it does not make the route safe to expose. The spawned brain keeps host networking by necessity.
findings.follow_up: MED-013-B: decide whether this service requires authentication, and if so route it through the same auth used for CRIT-007. Product decision, not a code fix.
findings.required_invariant: A request-reachable route must not spawn a process outside soul_sandbox, must not let caller-supplied text be parsed as an argument by the spawned program, and must bound how many processes a caller can create (INV-EXEC-1).
findings.remaining_exposure: The route has no authentication. `soul_cors` blocks a browser's cross-origin call but stops nothing that is not a browser, so any client with network access to the listener can spawn up to MAX_LIVE_BRAINS=16 python3 processes. That is a bounded denial of service rather than an unbounded one, and the spawned children are now seccomp-confined and rlimit-bounded, but the route is still an unauthenticated way to make this host run code it was configured to run. The brain also keeps host networking, necessarily: it exists to bind a port and answer on it.

fixing_prs.title: security(P1-8-B): sandbox the request-reachable spawn route, and add the argv API the sandbox was missing

findings.title: soul-kernel's is_safe_shell_command denylist does not block a newline, which sh treats as a command separator exactly like ';'
findings.discovered_by: P1-8-B, while routing the sh -c sites through the sandbox. Reading the existing 'security' check to see what it already covered is what turned it up; it is not in the original audit.
original_reachable_path: Action::ExecuteShell(cmd) -> is_safe_shell_command(cmd) returns true for a newline-separated payload -> Command::new("sh").args(["-c", cmd]) runs both commands
findings.required_invariant: A caller-supplied string must not be able to run a command the code did not intend, whether or not any particular metacharacter appears in a denylist (INV-EXEC-1).
findings.current_state: Fixed. `is_safe_shell_command` blocked `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, backtick, `$(`, `${` and `>` - but not a newline, which `sh` treats as a command separator exactly like `;`. So `"ls\nrm -rf /tmp/x"` passed the check and `sh -c` ran both halves. Verified directly: `sh -c "echo FIRST\necho SECOND"` prints both. `&` (background), `<` (input redirect) and `$'\x3b'`-style encodings were missed as well. The fix is not a longer denylist - the next missing character reopens it - but removing the shell: `Action::ExecuteShell` now executes through `soul_sandbox::Sandbox::execute`, which normalises encodings before matching, refuses `sh` as a head binary, and runs the command directly under seccomp and setrlimit. A separator the filter misses now has nothing to separate. `is_safe_shell_command` is kept as a cheap first pass, with a doc comment stating plainly that it is not the boundary, and a test that asserts the newline is STILL admitted - so anyone who later 'fixes' the list has to read why the list is not what holds.
findings.follow_up: Covered by the INV-EXEC-1 guard: a new spawn site fails CI unless it is sandboxed or explicitly allowlisted.
findings.residual_risk: None on this path once merged: `Action::ExecuteShell` no longer invokes a shell, so no separator - listed or missed - can start a second command. The class is not eliminated repo-wide. `soullink-actions`' `is_dangerous` and the orchestrator's own input checks are also denylists; they are now backed by the sandbox rather than relied upon, but any future site that adds a string filter WITHOUT routing through the sandbox reintroduces exactly this bug.

findings.title: ProvenanceLog's latest-per-record index was unbounded despite the ring's documented bound, and a lookup could not tell an evicted record from one never screened
findings.discovered_by: P1-6-B, while making provenance durable. Both defects are in code P1-6 added; neither is in the original audit.
original_reachable_path: AutonomousAgent::observe_untrusted -> record_provenance -> ProvenanceLog::record -> latest.insert (never evicted)
findings.required_invariant: A persisted memory record must remain distinguishable by trust level for as long as it exists, and the structures tracking that must be bounded (INV-MEM-3).
findings.current_state: Two distinct defects, both fixed. (1) UNBOUNDED INDEX. `ProvenanceLog` documented its ring as bounded 'so a long autonomous run cannot grow it without limit', and the ring was. The `latest` HashMap beside it was not: `record` inserted into it and nothing ever removed. A run re-ingesting distinct URIs grew it without limit, so the stated bound bounded nothing. Now capped at INDEX_CAPACITY (65536) with oldest-first eviction. (2) AMBIGUOUS LOOKUP. `latest_for` returned `Option`, and `None` meant both 'this content was screened and the note aged out' and 'this content was never screened' - which call for opposite decisions. Replaced at decision sites by `lookup`, returning Known/TrustOnly/Unknown. An evicted record keeps its TrustLevel, which is the field a caller acts on; the rest of a MemoryProvenance is explanatory. Durability: `ProvenanceLog::open`/`persist` write the index via temp-file-plus-rename, so a trust level survives a restart. A corrupt or version-mismatched index is an ERROR, not a silent empty start - starting empty would convert 'the provenance store is broken' into 'nothing was ever screened', which is the state INV-MEM-3 exists to prevent, reached by way of a failure nobody saw. MED-015-B closed both halves. WIRING: src/main.rs loads the provenance index at startup (data_dir/agent/provenance.json) and persists it after a one-shot `--ask`; an unreadable index REFUSES TO START in production (unknown mode = production posture) and warns in dev, because starting anyway would answer Unknown in silence and then persist a fresh index over the evidence. soul-daemon gained DaemonConfig::provenance_path — each per-goal agent loads the index before running and persists after, on failure too, since what the agent observed during a failed run is still evidence. TRUST FIELD: soullink-memory-hierarchy's MemoryEntry now carries a required `trust: MemoryTrust` ({Internal, Screened, Spotlighted, Derived, Unrecorded}) with serde-default Unrecorded, so pre-trust entries and silent writers cannot look clean. The compiler enumerated every construction site: agent-core's distillation writes are Derived (model output from a possibly-untrusted context), soul_entity's cycle observations are Internal, its public store_observation now REQUIRES the caller to declare trust, souls::brain::observe is explicitly Unrecorded (raw tool output, no screening on that path — labelled honestly rather than laundered). Consolidation takes the FLOOR of merged members' trust, so a merge cannot launder a Spotlighted member into a clean semantic summary.
findings.follow_up: MED-015-C: make recall/ranking consult MemoryTrust (at minimum, never re-inject Spotlighted content as instruction-bearing text), add trust to soul-memory's record shape, and route souls::brain::observe through a screening write path.
findings.residual_risk: The daemon's per-goal load-modify-persist means concurrent goals (max_concurrent_goals > 1) can interleave: the write is atomic so the index is never corrupt, but last-persist-wins can lose an overlapping goal's records — they come back Unknown, not wrong. Default is 1 concurrent goal. souls::brain::observe still writes raw tool output, now visibly labelled Unrecorded rather than fixed; routing it through a screening path is the real fix. soul-memory's own MemoryEntry (sled store) and the recall/ranking paths do not yet consult trust.
findings.remaining_exposure: Recall paths do not yet filter or rank by the new trust field, so a Spotlighted or Unrecorded record is retrievable exactly like an Internal one; the field makes the distinction durable and visible but nothing enforces it at read time yet. soul-memory's sled-backed MemoryEntry has no trust field, and the non-member trees construct hierarchy entries the workspace compiler cannot see.

findings.title: 27 sites attach a credential to an Authorization header as a plain String, invisible to a guard that matches on struct field names
findings.discovered_by: P1-5-C. Found by asking what is DONE with a value rather than what it is CALLED - the name-based scan structurally cannot reach these, because most are &str function parameters and locals, not struct fields.
original_reachable_path: a credential arrives as `token: &str` -> req.bearer_auth(token) / format!("Bearer {token}") -> outbound request
findings.required_invariant: A credential must be held in a redacting type and unwrapped only at the point of use, whatever the holding variable is named (INV-SEC-2).
findings.current_state: Confirmed and now VISIBLE, not fixed. P1-5-C added `plaintext_authorization_sites_do_not_grow`, which flags any value handed to `bearer_auth` or interpolated into a `Bearer`/`Bot`/`Token` header without `.expose()`. The check does not depend on naming at all: anything placed in an Authorization header IS a credential - that is what the header means - regardless of what the variable is called or whether it is a field, a parameter or a local. That is why it reached 27 sites the P1-5 field-name scan reported nothing about; MED-016-B has since migrated 8 of them, leaving 19. Only synergie's API currently does this correctly, via `token.expose()`. The budget is pinned two-way, so the set cannot grow and a fix must lower it. Verified negatively: adding one `bearer_auth(t)` call anywhere in a workspace member fails the test at 28. Not fixed in one change because migrating these means changing function signatures across a dozen crates; a flag day there would be churn rather than hardening, and the ratchet makes the exposure visible in the meantime. MED-016-B (first pass) migrated the two largest groups: soul_gateway's Slack/WhatsApp/Discord providers, whose tokens were `Option<String>` struct fields read from env, and avid-tui's five call sites, where one env-derived local was cloned into five async tasks. All eight now hold `SecretString` and call `.expose()` only at the header. `SecretString::is_empty` delegates to the inner value, so the providers' existing emptiness guards behave identically. The budget moved 27 -> 19 in the same change, and the ratchet's lower bound is what reported the new number: after the migration the test failed with 'only 19 sites remain but the budget is still 27'. Second pass (tranche 2) took the budget 19 -> 12: soullink-security's verify.rs (8 verifier functions), soullink-gateway's Slack and WhatsApp channels, its CLI `call` path and the OpenAI provider header. verify.rs was the instructive one - `Finding::secret` was ALREADY a SecretString, exposed at the dispatcher and passed as a plain `&str` into every verifier, so the type existed and was being discarded one frame too early. The verifiers now take `&SecretString` and expose only at the header or URL. The same file kept `checked: HashSet<String>` holding the EXPOSED text of every secret the scan had touched, purely to avoid double-checking; it now stores SHA-256 digests, which answer 'have I seen this' identically without retaining the credential. That was not one of the 27 counted sites - the scanner looks for Authorization attachment, not for retention - so it is a defect the guard could not have found. The retention check proposed after tranche 2 now exists: `exposed_secrets_are_not_retained_as_plain_owned_strings` scans for owned plaintext copies of exposed secrets (`.expose().to_owned()/.to_string()/.as_bytes().to_vec()`), sanctions copies wrapped in `Zeroizing::new` (they zero on drop - HIGH-001's own pattern), skips test modules, and pins the remainder two-way. It found exactly one member site: souls' settings TUI shows the stored API key as the editable 'current value' (souls/src/config.rs). That is recorded with a comment rather than silently fixed, because the fix is a UI decision - mask it or show set/unset - not a mechanical migration. A negative probe confirmed the check goes red on an unrecorded copy with file:line named.
findings.follow_up: MED-016-B (final): migrate the remaining 12 attachment sites. MED-016-C: decide the souls settings-TUI display (mask vs set/unset indicator) and clear RETAINED_EXPOSED_COPIES to empty.
findings.residual_risk: 12 attachment sites remain (unchanged - the hardest &str-parameter shape), plus the one recorded retention site in souls' settings TUI. The retention matcher is line-based: a copy split across lines, or made via a binding of the exposed &str that is owned later, is invisible to it. It narrows the gap the verify.rs HashSet fell into; it does not close every path to retention.
findings.reachable_from: Any outbound integration that authenticates: soul_gateway's Slack/WhatsApp/Discord providers, soullink-gateway's channel modules and OpenAI provider, soul_llm's OpenAI and Ollama providers, soullink-security's verify calls, avid-scout's auth, avid-tui's five API calls, ccos/eval, and src/main.rs. Each is reached whenever the corresponding integration is configured and used; none requires an attacker, because the exposure is the credential's in-process representation rather than a request an attacker sends.
findings.reproducer:
cargo test -p soulsystem --test architecture_secret_types plaintext_authorization_sites_do_not_grow -- --nocapture
prints all 27 sites with file and line. To confirm the check is live rather than vacuous, append `pub fn probe(c: reqwest::RequestBuilder, t: &str) -> reqwest::RequestBuilder { c.bearer_auth(t) }` to any workspace member's lib.rs and re-run: the test fails at 28 sites naming the new file.

findings.decision_required: Repository owners must decide whether to reverse the workspace-wide lint suppression. Reversing it under CI's -D warnings would convert an unknown and potentially very large number of currently-masked warnings across 184 workspace packages into hard build failures, so it needs an owner, a triage budget and a staging plan rather than an incidental change.
findings.required_invariant: The workspace build configuration does not globally downgrade dead_code, unused_imports, unused_variables and deprecated to allow.
findings.residual_risk: Genuinely dead or deprecated code, including orphaned security components (see HIGH-002), can accumulate without any build-time signal.
findings.follow_up: Owner decision, then a staged un-suppression: enable one lint at a time at warn level, triage, then promote to deny.

reachable_from: src/main.rs --plan flag -> soul_planner::CognitiveLoop::create_plan (reachable, produces an empty plan)
findings.reproducer: Run the binary with --plan '<multi-goal task>' and observe a Plan whose steps array is empty, because create_plan is called with an empty command slice and performs no LLM decomposition.
findings.required_invariant: Reachable plan generation and action decisions derive from the configured LLM or an explicitly documented deterministic strategy, not substring matching (INV-PLAN-5).
findings.residual_risk: The reachable damage is limited: run_react does its reasoning through the LLM and uses CognitiveLoop only for memory/history, so the keyword path is not load-bearing for the main agent loop. The --plan CLI surface still presents an empty plan as a result.
